title: sales-quick-hypercard-objections-draft
content:
Deck purpose:
- One-page, speaker-ready mini-deck (6–8 slides) for SDRs and AEs to carry into 1:1s and discovery calls.
- Focus: rapid objection handling and precise value framing against cost/latency/regulatory concerns.
- Design: minimal text, explicit scripts, 2 quick diagrams, 4 objection responses.

Slide 1 — Opening snapshot (what to say in first 30s)
- Title: "Lightning intro: what we do in one sentence"
- Script: "We help engineering teams run LLM inference with predictable latency and unit economics — across hosted, reserved, and private deployments — so they can ship features without building inference infra."
- Signal to watch: customer says "we already host models" -> pivot to ops costs and SLAs.

Slide 2 — TL;DR value (30s pitch for technical buyer)
- Bullet: Lower per-token cost via batching, cache, and quantization suggestions.
- Bullet: Reduce tail latency with smart routing and fallback models.
- Bullet: One API across hosted/dedicated/private for consistent rollouts.
- Speaker note: use numbers only if you have customer-specific workload (tokens/sec). Otherwise use ranges: "10–40% unit cost reduction typical for retrieval-heavy flows."

Slide 3 — 3 quick benefits for product/PMs (use case hooks)
- Benefit A: Faster time-to-market for LLM features (no infra backlog).
- Benefit B: Predictable pricing for forecasting (reserved capacity).
- Benefit C: Compliance-ready private deployments (VPC/KMS, audit logs).
- Quick ask: "Which of those is the most urgent for you right now?"

Slide 4 — Architecture mini-diagram (2 boxes + arrows, talk track)
- Left box: client app (requests) -> Router (policy: latency/cost/region) -> Serving pool (hosted / dedicated / private) -> datastore/cache.
- Callout: automatic prefix caching and model fallback keep app online during spikes.
- Speaker: point to "Router" and say: "We can route by cost or policy so critical flows hit dedicated pools, non-critical hit cheaper hosted variants."

Slide 5 — Four most common objections & micro-scripts
- Obj 1: "We already run models ourselves."
  - Script: "Totally — most teams we talk to own models but find maintenance and tail-latency engineering stays in-product teams. We benchmarked similar stacks and typically find a 30–50% ops time reduction after switching routing and caching policies. Could I share a short benchmark that maps to your infra?"
- Obj 2: "Cost — your API sounds expensive."
  - Script: "We treat cost as the primary product metric: batching, KV caching, and quantization guidance reduce per-token spend. For workloads with re-used prefixes (chat + retrieval) customers commonly cut spend by 20–40% — we can run a free cost-sanity exercise against a 24h sample."
- Obj 3: "Data security / compliance concerns."
  - Script: "We offer a Private deployment with customer-controlled VPC and KMS, plus audit logs. For regulated customers we also provide an on-prem install option and a SOC2-ready checklist; can I loop in our security lead for a 20-minute call?"
- Obj 4: "We need deterministic latency / SLOs."
  - Script: "Our Dedicated offering has SLA-backed targets and autoscaling policies that prioritize critical routes. We can run a short spike test against a reserved pool to quantify p95 improvements — want us to schedule?"

Slide 6 — Trap cards: competitor claims and responses
- Competitor: "They have cheaper vCPU-only endpoints."
  - Response: "Cheaper per-hour can hide higher per-token cost and unpredictable p95. We emphasize cost-per-output and tail behavior; can we compare token profiles?"
- Competitor: "We own the model, so latency is lower."
  - Response: "Owning a model is metric-agnostic; without routing, caching, and kernel selection you still see variance at production scale. We integrate with private models and show delta on p95 and cost."

Slide 7 — Pricing play (two quick asks)
- If cost is main blocker: offer a 30-day pilot with reserved capacity trial and a post-trial cost report.
- If security is main blocker: offer a joint security review + custom SLA proposal.
- Close script: "If I can get you a 30-day pilot with measurable latency and cost KPIs, would that help unblock?"

Slide 8 — Field checklist + next steps
- Checklist before demo: sample request logs (24h), target SLOs, compliance needs, decision timeline.
- Next steps template email (two lines): "Thanks — can you share 24h of request logs and the SLO you care about? We'll run a quick pilot plan and KPIs."
- Owner notes: assign to AE for pilot scoping and SE for security follow-up.

Appendix (one-pager attachments for AE/SDR)
- Short engineer-friendly datapoints: typical batch sizes, quantization options we recommend per model family, KV cache hit-rate examples from customer A.
- Links to internal artifacts: cost-calculator sheet, pilot-setup runbook, compliance checklist (Confluence IDs included above).

Open questions / TODOs for this draft
- Add a tiny benchmark image (p50/p95 before vs after) from our infra team (need results from infra/benchmarks).
- Validate the 20–40% cost claim with applied-ml team and replace with an anonymized case study.
- Create printable one-pager (PDF) for field events.

Speaker coaching notes (quick hits)
- Keep scripts concise; aim for 1–2 sentence answers to objections.
- Use leading questions: "Which of those two issues matters more for you: latency or cost?"
- If they push technical, switch to SE: "Great — can we loop your infra lead into a 30-minute spike planning session?"

End of deck — lightweight, field-ready, and purposely minimal for fast iteration.
